findings.title: Do not grant group management through the view scope
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this check, so an administrator granted only read access can create groups and move existing subgroups to the top level by posting their IDs. This permits unauthorized hierarchy changes, not just viewing. Require MANAGE here and add a negative test for group creation and movement with only VIEW.

findings.title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: The authorization resource ID is not the GroupModel ID: AdminPermissionsSchema stores the group ID as the resource name, while hasPermission() looks resources up by name. Both passing groupResource.getId() to that method and returning it as a group ID are incorrect. In particular, granting VIEW_MEMBERS on all groups causes this loop to return the synthetic Groups resource's UUID. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource then use that UUID as a membership filter, returning no users despite the grant. Resolve actual group IDs and handle the all-groups resource separately.

findings.title: Enable the group-member creation fallback for FGAP V2
findings.body: The group-member creation fallback still checks only the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature. With V2 enabled, an administrator granted MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP for a group, but not global user management, cannot create a user assigned to that group: requireManage() fails and this guard returns false before evaluating either group permission. Include V2 in this feature check so the newly implemented group scopes work for the existing group-member creation workflow, and cover this case with an integration test.
